reviews.text:
Thirsty Camel is such a vibe. We stopped in for drinks and small plates and ended up having one of the best bar experiences I've had in Scottsdale.
I ordered a Tito's soda and asked if they could make it a little fancy. They brought out prickly pear simple syrup and it was perfect. Light, refreshing, pretty, and exactly what I wanted.
We also had the Harissa Lamb Tacos and they were so good. Flavorful, tender, and balanced. The kind of food you order thinking it'll be just a snack and then you're mad you didn't order more.
But honestly, the service is what made this five stars. I accidentally left my credit card at the bar and the staff literally tracked me down, handed it back to me, and gave me a hug. That kind of care and attention is rare and really meant a lot. I wish I remembered the bartender's name because they were amazing.
Great cocktails, great food, beautiful setting, and genuinely kind people. I would absolutely come back and recommend this spot to anyone staying at or visiting The Phoenician
reviews.author: Kerbie D.

reviews.text: The lobby bar at The Phoenician was beautiful. We went to check out the tree lighting and stopped in to have a glass of sparkling rose. Prices are steep, but to be expected at a luxury property.  The bartenders were great too. Loved the decor.
reviews.author: Kim H.

reviews.text: art is truly the best! best service and very professional! he made it the best experience
reviews.author: M M.

reviews.text:
I visited The Thirsty Camel this past Tuesday afternoon and was very disappointed. After being seated on the patio and ordering cocktails, our server informed us that drinks would not be made unless a credit card was provided. Since the bar does not use portable payment terminals, the card had to be taken away from the table.

When the drinks were served, my card was not returned. Instead, I was told it would be held until we were finished, which I found unacceptable. Our server agreed to close out the tab immediately. We paid, had our drinks, and left.

Unfortunately, the drinks themselves were also underwhelming. They were just okay, and the lavender daiquiri--though presented in an attractive martini glass--was practically undrinkable because of the sharply curved lip. I had to pour it into my water glass just to manage it.

For a bar that positions itself as part of a high-end resort, requiring guests to hand over credit cards without secure, tableside payment options is both outdated and unprofessional. Coupled with mediocre drinks, the overall experience was disappointing.
reviews.author: Leslie C.

reviews.text: My typical experience here has been great,  however,  today I'm the only person of color here,  when I have my other I was asked for my credit card.  I gave it to her and said they have never asked me that before. I noticed other patrons that came in after me and they didn't ask one of them for there card.  This is an extreme example of racism.. it just doesn't stop.. do not single out one person because of race.  I will definitely write to corporate and see what happens..
reviews.author: Rod K.

reviews.text:
We stopped in while here for a dance event. 

Our server was Nicole (hopefully I remembered correctly) she was so kind and friendly! 

We had great little sampling of popcorn and pecans that were great. We had chips and salsa and both salsas were so good! 

They also have GF beer!
reviews.author: Brittney C.

reviews.text: Loved their drinks here and the ambiance during sunset is spectacular. The views, the service and the drinks are 5 stars! What I really want to ask for is their playlist outside? If it's not much to ask. I was vibin it.
reviews.author: Mycah S.

reviews.text:
We arrived in Phoenix this afternoon. Our room wasn't ready yet, so we went to one of the restaurants on the property.
We just wanted a cocktail and a snack. Raul was our server and he was great! He was a good server, but he was also fun.
We sat outside and enjoyed the fresh air, sunshine, and food and drink. Perfect way to start a vacation!
reviews.author: Melanie B.

reviews.text: What an amazing experience!!! We stop by as much as possible and usually stop in after visiting Mowry & Cotton on our way out of the hotel. The bar servers are so wonderful in their service and execution of everything. We always feel welcome and taken care of. I appreciate that we are never rushed and can relax at the bar. The live music makes for a lot of great memories. I can't say enough about the service and style of this oasis. Enjoy!
reviews.author: Doc H.

reviews.text:
Mad management. Comp a drink when you continue to make mistakes. 

Not the servers fault that they are under staffed. 

Shouldn't be mandating service charge when service is crappy
reviews.author: Robert B.

reviews.text: A great bar at the Phoenician hotel.  Lots of signature cocktails that were all quite delicious. My wife especially like the espresso martini, and I was a huge fan of the Negroni. They also have a good dining menu with a good selection of appetizers and entrées. Service was on the mark every time we went.  It is located in the center of the main lobby, so it is a great place to meet friends.
reviews.author: Mike S.

reviews.text: Thirsty Camel's afternoon tea, a treat so fine, finger sandwiches stacked, scones warm and divine. Devonshire cream, preserves, lemon curd too, each bite a delight, a feast for us two. Egg salad, chicken salad--both stole the show, had us savoring slowly, not wanting to go. Desserts to the brim, a sweet paradise, next time champagne? Now that would be nice!
reviews.author: Rhyme And D.

reviews.text:
Thirsty Camel is one of the best places to mellow out. There's live music pretty much every night. The ambiance  is very uplifting. The staff are all wonderful and experts in their crafts. 

Garage and valet parking available. Accessible.
reviews.author: O'Zandra F.

reviews.text: Seating is weirdly uncomfortable unless you get lucky to find pillows behind your back. Glass block overhead needs a good washing as well. Servers were very good, drinks are a good value for a resort. They don't open until 2 for drinks on a Saturday which was odd with many people looking for cocktails on vacation. Food service starts at 4. We asked for drinks that require a blender and were told they don't have blenders right now so we had to choose another drink. Firepits are nice at night at they do have heaters as well. Overall, it was okay but not a must do place to visit.
reviews.author: Janet B.

reviews.text:
Very tired out door patio. Old furniture that's uncomfortable, icky pillows, over priced drinks!!  Not very good snacks 
Wait staff was pleasant though!
Views just ok!!
reviews.author: Margaret O.

reviews.text: Great ambiance! Great drinks! Great service! Definitely suggest if staying at the Phoenician or visiting the area!
reviews.author: Nicole J.

reviews.text:
Destiny Brown is the subject of this review. She a must be the rudest manager on earth. She literally has no people skills and I don't know how she possibly became a manager. Read more for the whole story..

Due to extenuating circumstances, we ordered outside food but drinks from her restaurant. This is against restaurant policy but we discussed the situation at length with Andrew, the general manager. He understood and green lighted it. She then spoke in the most condescending manner in front of my kids. I honestly don't even talk to my 1st grader like that. I even told her I was recording her and she still couldn't control her attitude.

I asked her to get the other manager Andrew since he was already aware of our situation. She refused to and carried on berating me like I'm a child, vs a customer paying thousands of dollars to stay at this resort. Thank god andrew showed up and dismissed her from the situation.

1st night at the resort was a total buzz-kill. 
Literally going to bed before 10 pm bc of how uncomfortable it's been. 

For what it's worth the drinks were good.
reviews.author: Reggie W.

reviews.text: The most beautiful lounge inside and outside!! Bring your own of town guests for a five star experience on the patio with fire pits or on Saturday for afternoon tea. Book a cabana and make a day out of it!
reviews.author: Daria J.

reviews.text: Our group ordered cocktails and mocktails, all of which were tasty but very expensive, which is expected at a 5-star resort. The guacamole appetizer was very lackluster for the price. The presentation was beautiful but the food itself was bland and under seasoned. It also was brown and appeared to be sitting out for quite sometime. For $18+ I expect my guacamole to be made fresh.
reviews.author: Britney A.

reviews.text:
No reservation needed, seating inside and outside, does not validate parking like the other restaurants at the Phoenician. Valet is right next to it and takes tips. 

The cocktails are flavorful and strong. Queso Fundido was great. Strawberry Yuzu Cake fell short, cake was gritty and stale yet mousse was smooth.
reviews.author: Natasha A.

reviews.text: Amazing views, incredible drinks at a stunning resort... a great spot for sunset and patio vibes. Service was spectacular. We will be back!
reviews.author: Lindsey H.

reviews.text: Good ambiance and good service ,  we sat outside and it was a really nice Sunday afternoon
reviews.author: Eagle R.

reviews.text: Great atmosphere and fun vibe. Stood at an open area at the bar and old male bartender ignored me while got drinks for some old women, not even acknowledging me that he would be with me shortly.
reviews.author: Jennifer D.

reviews.text: A Bar is just a Bar, not here folks. Views are amazing, The drinks are generously poured. The seating is comfortable. The staff sets the bar of excellence one notch above excellent, why you may ask. My wife asked the waitress for recommendations for sights and dining in the area. The waitress replied with a couple options that were nice, what makes her exceptional is that she returned with a Map and list of places for us to visit. Who does that? That is what Is what I consider top tier service, when someone goes out of their way to provide information that does not directly effect them. To go above and beyond with nothing to gain. I wont provide her name because everyone at this spot is geared to provide an exceptional experience.
reviews.author: Manny G.

reviews.text: Great service, great drinks, kind staff. Lounge atmosphere with live music. Beautiful patio with spectacular sunset view!
reviews.author: E ..

reviews.text: Very solid bar with a great view. Paul the bartender provided me great recommendations and in definitely had a great time at the bar!
reviews.author: Alex G.

reviews.text: Being regular customers, we were both awed that a new design was in the midst a few years ago.  But after their revamp, I've grown accustomed to its new face!  It's a grand new and improved bar, not to mention all the finished redesign of the lobby, portico, restaurant and lounge - great job Phoenician!  The bar is perfectly set where bar folk look straight out to the panoramic view of our beautiful Valley of the Sun!  While waiting for our Phoenician Afternoon Tea, we were enthralled by the new design, layout and furnishings in the lounge area!  One has options to sit in modestly post-art deco modern-style seating - whether high top table or comfortable cushioned seating, or straight up at the bar.  This last time we visited, showed me their consistent and impeccable imbibing offerings.  Since construction was finished, we decided to visit a few more times - and for the most part, the Thirsty Camel is a gracious rejuvenation and design of a standard we really did not imagine could be done.  And the new environ is really conducive to 'lounging' and sipping any of their concoctions of which I must say, the Co-Pilot is a fabulous elixir - my better half preferred a very, very good Piper Sonoma Rosé Glass.  While my concoction was prepared with finesse, the glass was small - at least that's what my taste buds thought! Not to mention, their Co-Pilot; Yucca chips and pecans; or anything else available on the menu.  Go lounge!
reviews.author: Rick G.

reviews.text: Thirsty Camel is such a neat bar with gorgeous views of the valley. Come here at sunset and watch the sun go down with a nice cocktail and fire pit and you won't regret it. They also do afternoon tea which is so fun. The staff is wonderful. Raul at Thirsty Camel and Sabrina at Afternoon Tea are friendly and provide excellent service!
reviews.author: Zoe J.

reviews.text: This is a lovely bar with a great view of the Phoenician grounds. We sat at the bar once, and enjoyed afternoon tea on another day. Both times the staff were attentive, friendly, and quick. The views are beautiful, and the quality of the drinks and food are excellent. A great spot for a drink before or after dinner!
reviews.author: Vanessa B.

reviews.text: We just finished the best late night meal ever! The chipotle wings are soooooo good. Perfect crisp, flavor and the sauce omg! I found out the chef who makes the wings is Jilbert. So thank you Jilbert. My first time staying here at the Phoenician and visiting the Thirsty Camel and I will be back just for these wings!!! :)
reviews.author: Chloe F.

reviews.text: Outstanding service and top notch views. I always recommend this spot because the ambience is unbeatable and the food is just as amazing. Even if you want to enjoy a cocktail on the balcony and have a fully dinner somewhere else, there are three other restaurants in walking distance. One of my favorite places and I will always be back!
reviews.author: Maddy L.

reviews.text:
This was such a fun nightspot! We came here after eating at the Tavern restaurant. The short walk from the Tavern provided great views of the lush grounds. The pool view from the outdoor patio at Thirsty Camel was beautiful.

The large, outdoor fire pits provide lots of seating for different party sizes. And everyone seemed really friendly. When we first sat down, there were two people adjacent to us and two across from us. Both parties were welcoming and started a conversation with us. Then the two across left and four new people sat down and were friendly as well. Everybody seemed to be from different states and it was fun to share stories.

Inside was gorgeous as well; next time we may eat there instead of The Tavern.
reviews.author: Shawna H.

reviews.text: Beautiful evening with a great bar tender! Cheers to Chris! Loved the ambience and cocktails. Highly recommend
reviews.author: Jeff W.

reviews.text: The wine, cheesecake, and the view were stellar! They surprised us with the cheesecake and it was probably the best cheesecake I've ever had. Service was excellent and would definitely go back during cooler temperatures to sit outside.
reviews.author: Hanna S.

reviews.text: Great patio but if you want a draft beer  go elsewhere.  Service is slow and they are not very busy.  5 minutes after server poured my beer the foam finally settled.  (No, I haven't taken a sip yet.)
reviews.author: Bruce M.

reviews.text:
Our first time at thiis place and an adventure finding it.. the Phoenician Staff were so obliging where Siri was lost!
Super pretty views of the sunset..great ambience and our waiter Max was amazing.. funny friendly and quick!!!  Thank you so much!!  We will be back!
reviews.author: RO B.

reviews.text: Great spot for drinks with beautiful views of Camelback mountain. We were there on a Friday night and the live music was absolutely amazing. The guacamole and chips were delicious, as well, and we basically licked the bowl clean. We enjoyed sitting outside at one of the fire pits with our cocktails.
reviews.author: Jen B.

reviews.text: Gorgeous views, comfortable seating and delicious drinks! Everything you need. Staff was very kind and friendly, the bar snacks were also very good. Would definitely recommend to visitors and locals:)
reviews.author: Ann S.

reviews.text:
Nice friendly upscale bar within the Phoenician. Service is quick, attentive, and must say great pours. Love the pecan spicy snacks they bring, and prices are very reasonable for an upscale resort bar.  

Recommend sitting at the bar and enjoy the awesome view. 

Would give 5 stars as they should have a Happy Hour
reviews.author: William W.

reviews.text: Lovely spot with wonderful views of Phoenix. Nice drink selection of wines and cocktails as well as a few mock-tails offered on the menu. Our waitress explained they will make pretty much whatever you would like to order. They also have a small Sonoran inspired menu of bites to share, such as guacamole. Definitely a great spot to bring out of town visitors so they can enjoy views of the city.
reviews.author: Michele G.

reviews.text:
Ordered a corona and a cloud nine, had an amazing time and drinks were good until some racist chick on the way to the bathroom asked us if we were taking bags of food home for someone and started laughing with her friends. 

Not sure what would make her ask that except the fact that we were black and she and her friends were white. They were drunk as hell but it doesn't excuse racist behavior. We won't be back.
reviews.author: Tamika B.

reviews.text: Two local Phoenicians came here for birthday celebrations at the spa. Wow. What a disappointment on service. After being told to go to the pool, we were seated only to be kicked out and told to go to spa pool only (which we were NEVER told was upstairs). The spa pool was an awful slab of concrete with noisy generators and no ambiance. I will say, my service with Dawn was the best massage I've ever had! After massages, we went to Thirsty Camel so we wouldn't have to go back to the spa pool. Service here should be top of the line. Far from it. After 15 minutes with no service, we chose to order from the bar. Chris got us a glass of wine, but our cheese board NEVER arrived. We will definitely be returning to Camelback Inn spa by JW Marriott. Super disappointing at the Phoenician.
reviews.author: Lindsay S.

reviews.text: The Thirsty Camel got a new look and placement during The Phoenician's $90 million facelift. It used to be tucked away to one side of the lobby in an alcove and I think I remember some green marble being involved in the decor. Now it's front and center, taking up most of the glass wall overlooking the valley across from the entrance with a crisp off-white design scheme. I miss the old-school feel of the previous incarnation, but this version makes perfect sense and takes better advantage of the views. The cocktail list is extensive and the bartenders are always ready to work with you to customize something. They're occasionally a bit forgetful when you ask for water, but it's easy to forgive that gazing out across the grounds and the city with the mountains beyond.
reviews.author: Adam B.

reviews.text: Very peaceful place with good food and drinks, but the tortilla chips that came with my ceviche tasted like they were fried in very old oil
reviews.author: Alyona O.

reviews.text: The views off the  patio are BEAUTIFUL!! The hotel itself is very well appointed!  One of my fave vacay spots!!
reviews.author: Lisa N.

reviews.text: Waiter was incredibly attentive and went over the top. Dropping 1 star due to the bartender not putting in my order which caused a 20 min delay.   The steak fries were a square shaped which I have never seen before but created a perfect combo of crunch and soft inside = amazing! View is nice and the bar is conveniently located behind the lobby. The menu is small but there are alternatives for your bar needs.
reviews.author: Jeremy G.

reviews.text:
If you are here for the drinks the place is good, if you are staying at the hotel nothing like heading downstairs and having access to a full bar.

Drinks aside, I would not order the food, per one of the waiters he stated the best chicken sandwich was served here, sure i'll bite and against my better judgement try the best chicken sandwich made in AZ... To no surprise the sandwich was not best I have ever had or even close to the best I have ever had, stick to the mixed drinks and or straight pours the food is not something I recommend

drinks ****
food * best fried chicken sandwich in AZ, I highly beg to differ
price $$
service ****
ambiance **** modern
reviews.author: Clarence A.

reviews.text: The atmosphere was amazing, the views spectacular the dood and drinks were absolutely delicious. Our wait staff was superb.
reviews.author: Alecia R.

reviews.text: Meet the most rude waitress at The Thirsty Camel. Her name is Mandy and if she waits on you and you wish to have an enjoyable night without discrimination and being over charged and add drinks you did not order on your bill, then stay away from her. Everyone else was spot on but her.
reviews.author: Arden T.

reviews.text: Very nice. Interior was nice. The outside is where its at. It shows the pool area and views of the area. The fireplace is very nice.
reviews.author: Jason Y.

reviews.text:
They made good use of the space that was an outdated marble museum. When you walk in, there is a comfortable bar area. There are tables and seating groups. The service is decent. Enthusiastic older servers. There are outside tables to take advantage of the view vista. 

I only can imagine huge picture windows so that both inside and outside could take advantage of the view. 

Also, the band was good but much too loud.
reviews.author: Mike B.

reviews.text: Best margaritas I've ever, ever had. Packed full of "punch" with spice and flavor. Bartender is a true master mixologist and I've heard his products were manufactured and sold in local stores. Fantastic service, fun waiters and gorgeous renovation.  I will not return to Phoenix without visiting again.
reviews.author: Andrea S.

reviews.text: What a great Bar at the Phoeniciean! The bartender Chris is awesome!! Very personal, makes great drinks, very professional, takes his job seriously and a great personality! Will be going back! Had a great time!
reviews.author: Robin B.

reviews.text: You have to get a drink with Chris. He makes the best cocktails. My boyfriend and I searched near and far for a certain drink with no luck. Chris was able to create and perfect it!! He'll make you a great drink and he will remember your name.
reviews.author: Ryassal a.

reviews.text: Wonderful ambiance, extremely friendly and courteous staff. Outstanding drink menu. The views of the mountains were amazing. Very relaxing atmosphere. Tried the guacamole and ceviche appetizers, which were delicious! Will come back again.
reviews.author: Charlene M.

reviews.text:
As you would expect this is a fantastic venue to eat a drink, grab an appetizer or, just sit and gaze at the scenery. They are currently renovating parts of the facility, but the Thirsty camel is not effected. 

I'm a lover of old fashioned bourbon cocktails and their proprietary version is quite the treat. I highly recommend it!
reviews.author: Mitchell F.

reviews.text: Only had drinks at the lounge and sat out on the patio. Beautiful views and just a wonderful ambiance.
reviews.author: Timothy M.

reviews.text:
Went there the other evening to listen to my drummer pal, Joe Costello and his group.   Sat out on the balcony because the weather was perfect.   And check out the views of the pools.   Wow!!  Spectacular from above.   The coloring is what makes them pop.  

At first it was hard to get service.   My companion went to the bar twice to see if servers were even working the patio.   Yes, we were told.  An assistant brought us water as we waited and waited.   Maybe too much real estate to cover for two or three servers??

Hillary was our server.   She is very professional, personable, and knowledgable.  She showed up a little trick to "chill" the red wine.   Quite interesting and informative.

There are firepits -- which I didn't feel the need to use -- and comfy chairs as well as tables with chairs.   We chose a comfy couch.

Just peaceful up there.   So peaceful, in fact, that I was sorry we had to leave.

Either valet park or self park i the garage.   If self park, get a ticket from the server in order to get out of the garage.

I would definitely want to return.  And I'm looking forward to it.
reviews.author: Bonnie S.

reviews.text:
Come here for great view and ambiance, but expect overpriced food and drinks. 

Ordered:
1. DUCK CONFIT TACOS: 2/5 ehhh...not memorable at all
2. TIRAMISU: 3/5 better than my entree

Won't be coming back!
reviews.author: Jen H.

reviews.text:
I came to the Phoenician for a conference.  I stopped by the Thirsy Camel one evening for a quick dinner.  John, the bartender is great!  He knows what he is doing and is always ready to serve you!  His sidekick Robert is always ready to assist him when things get busy.  They're like the Ying and Yang of the Thirst Camel.  Look for them and you won't go wrong!  The avocado sushi was excellent.  Everything is fresh as expected from the Phoenician. If I'm not mistaken, they only have sushi available around the weekends.  They have a nice stock of beer, wine and spirits so feel free to have them mix you up something or create something of your own!  Excellent service and relaxing atmosphere, doesn't get any better.  

They only have one TV in the area for watching sports/news/etc that I can see.  So if the bar is crowded and have the TV behind you, watching can be difficult!
reviews.author: ben c.

reviews.text: What a relaxing way to end the evening...a cocktail in hand alongside Camelback Mountain with breathtaking views.  I was here on a Sunday evening with three other people.  We came here after dinner for a cocktail.  I have been here many times, but this was the first time in about 2 years.  Our waitress was professional and friendly, but did not write down our drink orders.  This was fine until she forgot what I had ordered.  She also said she would bring out waters on three separate trips to the table which never occurred.  I had a Mai Tai and it was excellent and worth the wait.  The service is usually much better.  Bring a jacket or sweatshirt as it can cool down at night and you are exposed to the wind.  There is nothing for enjoyable than having a beverage or two with soft music in the background.  We sat around a stone fire place in comfortable outdoor couches...perfect!  The lighting is dimmed and views are spectacular.  They do have a menu for appetizers and small plates as well.  Spoil yourself with a beverage here...it is worth it!  You can go here if you are not staying at the resort, but you do need to pay for parking.  Check out the walking paths behind the resort too...great for pictures!!!
reviews.author: Alex G.

reviews.text: Went into the Thirsty Camel on Wednesday and was greeted instantly with warm smiles and welcomes. Went to the bar and was helped out by Robert and Ashley B. Both were very knowledgable and extremely friendly! The resort was busy for midweek, seemed like there was a few corporate groups. Highly recommend going in!
reviews.author: Micaela C.

reviews.text:
My husband and I spent a weekend at The Canyon Suites last month, and came by the Thirsty Camel for drinks on both the Friday and Saturday nights. It was a nice hotel bar, with indoor lounge and bar seating, a big outdoor patio, and a lovely view. A great spot for a nightcap if you're staying at The Phoenician.

The vibe was upscale but relaxing--you would never confuse the Thirsty Camel for anything other than a hotel bar. We spent one night next to a large group of loud middle-aged white people on some kind of company retreat. I overheard one of the women proclaim proudly, "Anyone who offends me who's a woman is a whore." Her male friends were super amused by that. Service was good. I appreciated that there was table service all night. The staff was attentive, even when we were sitting outside. They set us up with tasty bar nuts and brought our cocktails in good time.

The drinks were decent, nothing thrilling, but definitely solid. I enjoyed the Triple S, a spicy tequila cocktail made with El Tesoro Blanco, agave nectar, jalapeño, watermelon, and lime, with a hickory smoked-salt rim. The Phoenix Rising was apparently the signature cocktail, and this was good, made with Woodford Reserve bourbon, cointreau, orange juice, Angostura and Fee's orange bitters, grenadine, and orange peel. The Thirsty Sazerac was a serviceable sazerac, mixing Bulleit rye with green chartreuse, brown sugar, Angostura and Fee's lemon bitters, and lemon peel. If you're feeling spendy, the Five Diamond Manhattan is a well-made $20 Manhattan with Woodford Reserve, Carpano Antica, and Fee's barrel-aged bitters.

I doubt I'd drink here if I weren't staying at this hotel, but that's kind of the great thing about hotel bars. They're luxurious but unfussy, easy to visit before slipping off to bed. I really like The Phoenician and The Canyon Suites, and if I have occasion to visit again, I'm sure I'll be back for another round at the Thirsty Camel.
reviews.author: Steph C.

reviews.text: Great service and love the Pheonician. I had the Manhattan and wife had spicy margarita. Both drink put together really well. Again the staff is top notch.
reviews.author: Frank S.

reviews.text: Overpriced wine, only a view for atmosphere.Why do they think their $10 bottle wine is worth $18.00 glass....?....greed greed greed
reviews.author: dan h.

reviews.text: Very nice place. One of the best. Really liked our stay and my stop into the Thirsty Camel. We had the place rented out for a party. Nice band and good drinks. All the food was good. For sure would come back.
reviews.author: Joe M.

reviews.text: We love visiting this restaurant for an evening out on the town for natives or for visitors! It is the perfect place for coffee and dessert, drinks and music, or just dinner! The views are gorgeous just to top it off. Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Jennifer R.

reviews.text: Whatever thirsty camel shows up here for a drink or some better have some serious moolah.  As a NYer, I am used to $15-16 per drink, but that doesn't mean I'm too crazy about it. You are essentially paying for the view and the honor of sitting your rear end at a bar in a resort that runs upward of $700 per night.
reviews.author: Rich J.

reviews.text:
I absolutely love this place.  For a fantastic view and a great glass of wine, it can't be beat.  The atmosphere is excellent.  I put this place on the same level as the lounge at Pelican Hill in Newport Beach.  

The bartender we had was Shawn and he actually remembered us from the previous year we were there which was impressive.  I give 5-stars to Shawn as well.  We tried a couple of different wines and also a specialty drink that he recommended which we found to be terrific.  We also ordered a plate of hummus which was done well although it could have used more flatbread to accompany it.  Shawn did however quickly retrieve more of that for us.  

For anyone looking to start out a weekend evening in Scottsdale, I highly recommend this lounge because it satisfies several elements that people who are used to a nice, sophisticated environment that also has energy tend to seek out.
reviews.author: Charles C.

reviews.text:
Tea time? Ice Cream & Sorbet time? Creme Brulee time? Relaxing-the night time? It's all here!

This has a been one of the fav spots lately for our group's tea time after dinner, or ice cream, or dessert, or just to enjoy the nice night view with some great live music! The house-made vanilla and chocolate ice cream is amazing! And the selection of different sorbets are so delicious (have been offered a few different flavors on multiple  trips). As the weather is starting cooling down, I can see an increasing number of trips!!

The only drawback is that service seems always to be slow. There were a couple of times there was only one waitress for the entire patio and it took 30 mins just to pay, so have a little patience if that is your case.
reviews.author: Ziyu W.

reviews.text:
Great live music. Beautiful scenic views. The best service in town.  Sounds great--right?  My husband and I recently stayed at the Phoenician and made visiting the Thirsty Camel a nightly ritual.  The beer and liquor selection is excellent and the apps are great (try the dip trio!).  The prices are a little high (I recommend having a happy hour!) but the experience is worth it.

Bottom line:  Will we be back?  Gosh! I sure hope so:)
reviews.author: Sarah J.

reviews.text: Amazing views of the Valley and well mixed drinks, but the service is always a little slow.
reviews.author: Jennifer S.

reviews.text:
Came to meet a friend for happy hour on a Friday.  It was around 6ish and had to wait about 10 minutes to get into the resort.  The Phoenician had a information stand as you drive into the resort and the greeter stopped every car to ask where they were going.  It backed up everything which made me late meeting my friend.  It was so ridiculous.  Anyhow, once the greeter gave me my valet pass I could finally make it up to the resort.

We sat outside and the view was beautiful.  They had a live band playing at the pool which we could hear BUT they also had a guitar player in the lounge inside the Thirsty Camel.  So, when the door was open you had two different style of music playing.  

Anyhow, our waitress was awesome, great wine selection, we ordered a veggie appetizer which was good.  After two glasses of wine and my friend and I split the  veggie appetizer, I was in for 50 bucks.  

I won't do this every Friday, but it was nice because in those few hours I felt I was on vacation.....once I got pass the information stand/greeter.
reviews.author: Mel G.

reviews.text: Perfect view, yummy drinks, great musician, and a book is a lil attainable slice of heaven! No much needed to be written...
reviews.author: Eboniña E.

reviews.text:
Let's be honest: the number one reason to come here is the view on the patio. Kicking back on a loveseat around the firepits with a cocktail and some snacks... It doesn't get much better. 

All of the drinks we tried were solid. No one standout, but just well-mixed drinks. Extensive tequila and liquor selection in general. Didn't get to try much food, but the crab dip appetizer one night really hit the spot. 

Being able to light up a cigar outside just completes the experience.
reviews.author: Greg H.

reviews.text:
The food is really good. Nice wine and alcohol selection. To top it all of, the wait staff is super super nice.

The ambience is just like any other run of the mill hotel bars. The outside sitting does compensate a lot for the generic ambience.
reviews.author: Ayon J. R.

reviews.text:
How do I love thee Thirsty Camel? Let me count thy ways...

1) The scenery rocks!
2) Love going to a resort for a nightcap, makes me feel like I'm on vacation
3) The service is typically top-notch (ask for Kaylyn)
4) Great little snackies - cashews, wasabi peas, etc
5) Ambiance of a luxury resort
6) Getting discounts on Restaurant.com
7) Getting SPG points for my purchases here...
8) Close to home
9) The food is pretty good - - kobe burger is great!
10) The bellinis..... ohhh, the bellinis!
reviews.author: Jessica A.

reviews.text:
This place was great!  The view was gorgeous and the food was just as good, corn dogs with truffle ketchup, Yum!  
There was any sort of alcohol, wine, and beer you could ever want which is always a good thing to me!  
The only problem was the service.  It was really slow...  Our waitress made up for it though!  She bought us two amazing deserts paired with a delicious desert wine.  
I will definitely be back!
reviews.author: Amy E.

reviews.text: I just love coming here when I am in Scottsdale!  Prefer to sit outside on their terrace that overlooks the city in the evening when they have their fire pits going.  Just a few cocktails and an appetizer or two can set you back some bucks but hey, every once in a while you got to treat yourself!
reviews.author: Karen O.

reviews.text:
Since this bar was right outside the door of my room, I happen to make several visits.  Most of them were very positive.

Most of the bars at the Phoenician will make a good mojito.  This place makes the best.  It is one of the best mojitos I had in a long time.

The bar is very nice.  Looks like something you would find in San Francisco.  Very large marble bar with high bar stools and very nice furnishings and a large out-door area for sitting and relaxing, especially toward dusk.

The bar also has a fine selection of cigars.  I don't think you can smoke there.  I did not eat at the bar.  They did serve a selection of tasty nuts though.

The staff was pretty friendly, except for one young guy.  I guess he just got hired or something.  That guy made a big deal about two of my guest not wearing sleeves?  Not like we are in the UAE or Saudi Arabia!  Any way, did not make a big deal since my room was next door, but still kind of weird.  I know it is a 5-star hotel, but it is summer, the pool is right out the door and they were wearing nice tank-tops.  What ever.  I still liked the bar.

If you need to make a choice in hotels, this is the place!
reviews.author: John O.

reviews.text:
I'm giving this place 4 stars (and not 5) simply because the drinks are  f-ing expensive.  The seafood risotto just may be the best meal south of Camelback Mountain.  Believe it or not, for $32, it's a bargain - it comes with lobster tail, scallops, shrimp, and of course risotto.

Unlike many other high end eateries, you will not walk away feeling hungry.  The bartenders at Thirsty Camel are all top notch and friendly.  Jeff, Scott, and Kyle are sure to take care of your every need.  The people come from all over the country, conversation is never dull, and the views certainly don't suck.

You can't go wrong at the Camel - if you're looking for a piece of ass, there are sure to be many a cougar on the prowl at this joint.  On the other hand, if you're looking to wine and dine your date, this is a great hotel bar to check out.  Who knows, if you get lucky, some of the nicest rooms in town are a few steps away.
reviews.author: Jared M.
